summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR128 crore; FY26 EBITDA margin 18.8% as Raipur ramp-up weighed, with FY27 guidance of 15% revenue growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR128 crore (up 24% YoY), with EBITDA of INR25 crore (19.5% margin) and PAT of INR14.7 crore (11.4% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR478.5 crore, EBITDA INR90.1 crore (18.8% margin) and PAT INR42.2 crore (8.8% margin). The newly commissioned Raipur hospital lost INR13.8 crore of EBITDA in FY26 and held occupancy at about 12% for the year, while mature hospitals delivered INR103.9 crore EBITDA at a 23.06% margin. Management guided to 15% revenue growth, around 8% ARPOB growth and roughly 100 bps EBITDA margin expansion in FY27, with Jamshedpur (150 beds) due by Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Raipur EBITDA loss in Q4 about INR3 crore

segments.name: Salt Lake (flagship, tertiary and robotics)
segments.commentary: Occupancy rose from 58% to 63% in FY26 (about 68% per Q&A), ARPOB INR43,800 in Q4 vs INR39,300; LOS 3.06; over 800 robotic surgeries in the year. Guided to 70-73% for FY27.

segments.name: ILS Dumdum
segments.commentary: Restructured specialty mix; occupancy about 70% in Q4 (from mid-60s), ALOS down to 4.47 from 4.59. Around 30 cardiac surgeries in one quarter. FY27 guide 72-73%.

segments.name: ILS Agartala
segments.commentary: Occupancy 42% to 52% in Q4 YoY; hospital grew about 18%. Bangladesh share of volumes fell to about 3% from about 10%. ARPOB intentionally discounted; guided +7-8% YoY. FY27 occupancy target about 58%, with about 100 beds addable at 70% occupancy.

segments.name: ILS Howrah
segments.commentary: Occupancy 39% to 47% in Q4 YoY; around 100 robotic knee replacements in just over a year. Guided to late 50s for FY27 and about 60% by Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Raipur (commissioned May 2025)
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 12.35% for FY26 and 14.26% in Q4; revenue about INR3.5 crore in ~10.5 months. Monthly EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q3 FY27 at about 25% occupancy; FY27 exit occupancy about 30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15% YoY (management also referenced FY27-FY28 at 15%).
FY27 EBITDA margin expected to rise about 100 bps, to around 20.2%, with Jamshedpur losses absorbed.
ARPOB growth of about 7-8% in FY27 from tariff changes and specialty optimisation; Jamshedpur ARPOB in mid INR35,000.
Raipur monthly operational breakeven targeted by Q3 FY27; full-year FY27 Raipur result expected at about breakeven, fully positive in FY28.
Jamshedpur 150-bed hospital to be commissioned by Q4 FY27 at about INR70 lakh per bed capex; about 90% of capex to be deployed in FY27, balance via creditors.
Agartala ARPOB to rise but stay below Kolkata units; Agartala occupancy expected near 60% by early FY28.
capex_capacity: Jamshedpur 150-bed tertiary hospital on schedule; commissioning targeted by Q4 FY27; capex about INR70 lakh per bed, similar to Raipur.
About 90% of Jamshedpur capex to be spent in FY27; remaining about 10% to be settled via creditors in FY28.
Agartala has vacant land; about 100 beds can be added once occupancy reaches about 70%. Older Kolkata hospitals have no real estate for bed expansion.
Raipur has added renal transplants (6 done) and received liver transplant licence; PET and linear accelerator at Agartala.
Management is evaluating greenfield and M&A in Eastern India, typically 150-200 bed hospitals; no deal announced.
demand_pricing: Raipur insurance empanelments delayed (typically about 15 months for new hospitals); expected to complete in the next quarter. Raipur patients mostly cash at present, so ARPOB is elevated and may fall 4-5% after empanelment and corporate onboarding.
Payer mix: about 90% of revenue from cash and insurance (roughly 50:50 split); corporate about 5%, scheme (Ayushman Bharat etc.) about 5%.
West Bengal government change: Ayushman Bharat to replace Swasthya Sathi; management does not expect a notable ARPOB impact.
Bengal elections caused a slight footfall impact in Q4 FY26 and a larger impact in April 2026 (Q1 FY27).
Management cited Chhattisgarh bed density of about 1.15 per 1,000 and sees room for new entrants alongside incumbents.

qa_highlights.question: How soon will Raipur occupancy reach the desired level?
qa_highlights.answer: Hospital commissioned mid-May 2025, about 10.5 months of operation, revenue about INR3.5 crore at about 15% occupancy. Optimum occupancy expected by Q3 FY27; hospitals typically take 24-36 months to break even monthly.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year Raipur result and FY27 occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Slight loss for FY27 near breakeven, fully positive in FY28. Year-end FY27 occupancy about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Raipur ramp slower than hoped?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance empanelments delayed; expected to complete next quarter. Management says performance could have been better without the delay.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the loan to a body corporate in the cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in a company at a pre-set coupon, expected to be fully wound up within FY27. Management said there are no related-party transactions across group companies.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA growth lag revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects EBITDA margin up about 100 bps, after absorbing Raipur breakeven and Jamshedpur set-up losses; FY27 margin about 20.2%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Dum Dum occupancy down, and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Restructuring to decentralise specialties and add cardiac, interventional radiology and neurology; occupancy back to about 70% in Q4 and guided to 72-73% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Salt Lake occupancy figure consistent with the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would check. The presentation showed 62.4% for Salt Lake versus about 68% cited on the call.

risks_watch: Raipur ramp-up depends on insurance empanelments and the 25% occupancy breakeven; watch Q1-Q3 FY27 occupancy and monthly EBITDA.
Jamshedpur commissioning by Q4 FY27 and ramp-up to 10-14% occupancy in year one; EBITDA dilution from pre-opening losses.
Margin dilution: FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 18.8% from 22.1% in FY25 due to Raipur.
Agartala depends on Bangladesh patient flows (about 3% of volumes now vs about 10% earlier); recovery timing uncertain.
Bengal election disruption in Q1 FY27; Ayushman Bharat transition; nursing attrition at new hospitals.
Loan to a body corporate in cash flow, which management says will be wound up in FY27.
Salt Lake occupancy figure discrepancy (presentation 62.4% vs about 68% on call) pending clarification.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on mature-hospital momentum, Dum Dum recovery and Agartala/Howrah trajectory, with specific numerical targets for FY27. More defensive on Raipur, attributing the slower ramp to delayed insurance empanelment, and on the Salt Lake occupancy figure, which was not reconciled on the call.
key_quotes: We expect optimum occupancy levels to be reached by quarter 3 of this year.
We expect the ARPOB to grow by around 8% through a mix of tariff increase as well as specialty optimization.
Insurance empanelment's generally take around 15 months for any new hospital.
I think 100 basis points increase after a setup of the initial loss of Raipur is not conservative.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 15% with ARPOB up 7-8% and ~100 bps margin expansion; the 150-bed Jamshedpur hospital (INR70 lakh/bed, about INR105 crore) is due by Q4 FY27 and mature-hospital occupancy ramps to 70-73% at Salt Lake and Dumdum, but no capacity adds beyond Jamshedpur and the Raipur ramp are specified for the 15% growth.
